chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When they see the crescent before midday, it is for the previous night, and when they see it after midday, it is for the coming night."

And that which was narrated - Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Abu Talib 'Abdullah ibn al-Salt from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah and 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When the crescent is seen before midday, that day is from Shawwal, and when it is seen after midday, that day is from the month of Ramadan."

So these two reports are also among those from which it is not valid to object against the apparent meaning of the Quran and the mutawatir reports, because they are not well-known (ma'lum), and that which has this ruling is not necessarily resorted to. Moreover, if they were sound, it would be permissible that the intended meaning of them is: when two witnesses testify to its sighting before midday, it is obligatory to rule that that day is from Shawwal. And no one should say that if this were the intended meaning, there would be no benefit to its sighting before midday, because whenever the two witnesses testify, it is obligatory to act upon their word, because that is only obligatory if there is a doubt in the town and they did not see the crescent. And the meaning of these two reports is that there is no doubt in the town, but they made a mistake in sighting the crescent, then they saw it the next day before midday, and their sighting was accompanied by the testimony of the witnesses, so it is obligatory to act upon it.

And that which indicates that whenever it is independent of the testimony of the witnesses, it is not obligatory to resort to it, even if it is seen before midday, is what was narrated: Ali ibn Hatim from Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who said: I wrote to him (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, sometimes the crescent of the month of Ramadan is obscured from us, so the crescent is seen the next day before midday, and sometimes we see it after midday. Do you think we should break the fast before midday if we see it, or not? And how do you order me in that?' So he wrote (peace be upon him): 'You complete until the night, for if it is complete, it is seen before midday.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sighting the crescent before or after midday for determining the start of a lunar month?
ai.summary: This passage from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* explores the jurisprudential nuance of lunar crescent sighting, specifically addressing the ambiguity that arises when the moon is sighted before or after midday (*zuwal*). Al-Tusi critically analyzes these reports, noting their limited authority compared to the Quran and *mutawatir* traditions, and clarifies that the timing distinction primarily applies when there is no local doubt (*illa*) in the town, ensuring that the ruling aligns with the certainty of the month's completion or beginning.
